title: The 3-Step Work Test Before You Buy

beats.say: Before you buy it, turn the price into hours of your work.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a price tag fluttering on a dark jacket under harsh sodium light.

beats.say: Most people look at a $100 price tag and see a number. But what is it really costing you?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a towering concrete office building cutting into a cold blue hour sky.

beats.say: Step one. Work out your exact take-home pay per hour after taxes.
beats.visual: A hand sliding a blank paper across a dark wooden desk under a single practical lamp.

beats.say: Step two. Divide the price of the item by that hourly rate.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of an empty highway stretching into a foggy industrial ridge line at night.

beats.say: Step three. Ask yourself if the item is truly worth those hours of your life.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a lone person standing against a vast expanse of open dark water.

beats.say: Suddenly, a $100 impulse buy costs you 4 full hours sitting in a stuffy office.
beats.visual: Wet asphalt reflecting cold fluorescent lights in an empty downtown underpass.

beats.say: Is trading 4 hours of your breathing life for a shirt actually a fair trade?
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a heavy brass clock hand ticking past an unlit index mark.

beats.say: Most folks assume money just disappears. But your paycheck is stored time.
beats.visual: High angle shot of rain-slick pavement under a solitary flickering street lamp.

beats.say: When you view purchases through hours worked, the urge to spend quietly fades.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking away down a long, narrow industrial corridor at dusk.

beats.say: Try this math on your next purchase and drop the item in the comments.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a dark keyboard with a single pool of light catching the keys.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary tower edge cutting through heavy fog at dawn.

caption: Turn any price into hours worked before you spend a dime. #moneypsychology #personalfinance #smartspending #budgeting
description: Stop looking at dollar signs. Use this simple three-step work test to price purchases in hours of your life.
first_comment: What is the last thing you bought measured in hours of work?

facts.claim: Price items in hours worked to evaluate true cost

loop_map.stakes: A $100 purchase measured in hours of work.
